summary: A 120-foot steel tower was erected at Knightdale in 1938; it was taken down in 1972 and a source says it went to South Mills, where no source confirms it stands.

facts.design: 120-foot International-Stacey steel tower with an inside stairway
facts.status_note: Taken down in 1972 and stored in Clayton; a source says it was later moved to South Mills, Pasquotank County, but no source confirms it stands there now.

events.note: Tower site acquired from Meredith College trustees; 120-foot steel tower erected. The lookout history says the CCC erected it on November 23, 1938.
CCC side camp completed a four-room frame house at the tower.
Tower taken down and stored in Clayton.
Tower later moved to South Mills, Pasquotank County; the source gives no date for the move.

evidence.supports: The tower was a 120-foot steel tower erected in 1938 and the lookout history says the CCC erected it.
The tower was erected on November 23, 1938, from a CCC side camp.
evidence.quote: erected November 23, 1938, from Side Camp S-68.

evidence.supports: The tower had an inside stairway and stood at Knightdale in Wake County.
evidence.quote: 120 foot steel tower, inside stairway, located at Knightdale in Wake County

evidence.supports: A CCC side camp completed a four-room frame house at the tower in February 1940.
evidence.quote: 4-room frame house at Knightdale tower in Wake County

evidence.supports: The tower site was acquired from Meredith College trustees.
The site was on the east side of Hester Street.
The tower was an International-Stacey steel tower.
The house and site were sold in 1971.
The tower was removed in 1972 for storage in Clayton.
evidence.quote: 1972 - Tower removed, for storage in Clayton and subsequent

evidence.supports: The tower was later relocated to South Mills, Pasquotank County.
evidence.quote: relocation to South Mills, Pasquotank County

notes_for_editor: The 1971-1972 history and the South Mills move come from one local history page, which gives no date for the move and no builder. The CCC attribution rests on the eastern lookout page alone. A search snippet said a WRAL report called the Knightdale tower torn down 30 years ago; the WRAL page at https://www.wral.com/story/20865568/ that was fetched is about a north Raleigh tower and does not mention Knightdale, so the claim is not used. Location conflict in the brief: tnlandforms gives 35.78611, -78.46138 and the eastern page gives 35.7863, -78.4778, about 1.5 km apart; the story makes no location claim. No staffing source was found.
